post.summary: Situation 2 · Needs her yes, Instant club
post.description: Leaves a game needing only the protagonist's yes, at a club that books at once: the soonest card of hers in the group and sport that her deck shows — one with 2 hours left before its book-by, where there is one — with enough of the people dealt it beside her saying yes — each through the yes their own phone runs. Her yes then fills it: a charge, *It's a game!*, then Home. With no such card, the proposer deals first.

post.summary: Situation 3 · Needs her yes, On request club
post.description: Situation 2 at a club that confirms each game: her yes asks the club, and the club row accepts or refuses — or the club's time to confirm runs out. **With `answer_due_in_minutes`, the club is asked already**: her game at the soonest hour an On request club of the group's sells, made and said yes to by her and three of the group — hers last — as if earlier, so the answer is due that many minutes from now (or, past the club's own time to confirm, that long from now); then *Run it now* on the club's answer window calls it off once it is due.

SearchMode.title: SearchMode
SearchMode.description:
What kind of game this is. **Two values, never three.**

``PlayIntent`` is a player's declaration and has three values; this is the
*game's* kind — a Games card is competitive or for fun — and has two. The
arities differ on purpose, so the likeliest bug in reading one as the other
is a type error rather than a paragraph in a document.

It picks the level window's tolerance (``matchmaking/domain/level_window.py``)
and nothing else here.

waiting_for_the_club.title: Waiting For The Club
waiting_for_the_club.description: This yes filled the game at an **On request** club: it went to the club, which confirms it within its time to confirm, and nobody pays until it does — the charge and *It's a game!* follow its yes. The game is on Home as `WAITING_FOR_THE_CLUB`.
